A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scSplit research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including content relocated or regrouped in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original microscopy unmixing and bleedthrough-removal experiments, downstream segmentation results in Table 4, and a GoPro deblurring experiment in Appendix J.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results, including the microscopy benchmarks, segmentation evaluation, and supplementary GoPro experiment.

M1.justification: The two generators, mixing-ratio regressor, SCIN normalization, arithmetic-mean aggregation, training objectives, and one-step inference are retained. Wording and notation refinements do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The five microscopy datasets, downstream segmentation task, and GoPro experiment remain. However, Section 4 changes the HTT24 channel pair from SOX2 versus MAP2 to SOX2 versus Golgi while retaining its displayed examples and scores. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects the description or changes the underlying task selection.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain U-Net, the three µSplit variants, denoiSplit, MicroSplit, InDI, and scSplit variants. The instance-normalization, augmentation, and precision comparators were already evaluated in v2, including its appendices.

E3.justification: The stated mixing regimes, preprocessing, patch sizes, training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Figure S.19 still specifies 2,000 randomly sampled 512×512 image pairs. Table 3 revises a predicted mixing ratio rather than specifying a new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure S.19 revises the empirical curves examining how normalization affects patch-standard-deviation dependence on mixing ratio across Hagen, HTLIF24, and BioSR. The diagnostic question and qualitative conclusion remain unchanged; the other ablations and robustness investigations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains the same frame-based standard-error methodology, and Tables S.9–S.10 retain their uncertainty values. Existing error bars remain. Figure S.19 concerns input variability and does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes scSplit's estimated t_agg for HTT24 (1:4) from 0.82 to 0.25, while retaining PSNR 35.6, SSIM 0.955, and LPIPS 0.020. Figure S.19 also contains modestly different numerical curves. The remaining matched performance tables and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly uses random-pixel variables p0 and p1, aligning its notation with the existing Appendix A derivation. The mathematical reasoning, assumptions, and formulas are retained; the variance-symbol correction in appendix prose is not a substantive theoretical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that severity-aware normalization, mixing-ratio estimation, and aggregation enable one framework to address image unmixing and bleedthrough removal. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contribution and applicability claims.

C2.justification: The segmentation discussion drops the assertion that its findings perfectly correlate with PSNR, retaining the narrower observation that scSplit gives the closest segmentations. The expanded normalization discussion reiterates a limitation already described in v2's Table S.8 caption; the principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit source-code and pretrained-model repository location to the abstract. This improves access information, although repository availability was not externally verified. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and positioning relative to InDI and earlier semantic-unmixing methods remain unchanged. Reference renumbering does not add literature, and the additional normalization critique repeats an argument already present in the earlier appendix.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited paragraph and heading edits, clarifies aggregation and segmentation descriptions, repairs several supplementary cross-references, and updates author and publication-status text. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 combines v2's Figure 4(a) and Figure 2 into Figure 4, with the remaining regression panels becoming Figure 3. It places Tables 2–3 together, improves qualitative-panel labels and some legends, relocates Figure S.19, and places Figures S.20–S.21 on one page.

improvement.justification: The direct code/model location, clearer figure labels and cross-references, revised Table 3 annotation, and more restrained segmentation interpretation modestly improve usability and reporting precision. The scientific method and performance evidence remain largely stable; the unresolved HTT24 channel-description change limits confidence in that particular revision.
